validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION confirmed at high tier. This is the Phase 2 (Line 300) component of a real, FERC-certificated project: Driftwood Pipeline LLC applied June 17, 2021 (Docket CP21-465-000; Federal Register notice July 7, 2021), proposing dual 42-inch NGA section 7(c) transmission pipelines from near Ragley (Beauregard Parish, LA) to a receiver facility near Carlyss (Calcasieu Parish, LA); FERC issued the Final EIS Sept. 2022. The operator's own project page (Wayback-captured, live site now dark) breaks the project into 'Line 200 - Phase 1' (36.9 mi, 2.4 Bcf/d) and 'Line 300 - Phase 2' (32.4 mi, approximately 4.6 Bcf/d) -- this row is Phase 2 specifically, matching the sheet's 32.4 mi / 4600 MMcf/d exactly. Not a hallucination or GEM-only entity.

DUPLICATE check against the batch's flagged Driftwood family (P0177/P3282/P7769/P7770): P0177 Mainline is the ORIGINAL, separate FERC docket CP17-117/CP17-118 (certificated 2019, 96 mi, 4000 MMcf/d, Ville Platte -> Carlyss) feeding the LNG terminal itself -- a different project. P3282 is Phase 1 (Line 200, 36.9 mi, 2400 MMcf/d, same CP21-465 docket, now under construction per EIA). P7769 is very likely Phase 3 (Line 300 continuation, ~69.3 mi per EIA's Aug2026 release, 1000 MMcf/d, same CP21-465 docket) -- see cross_row_leads. All four are physically and administratively distinct scopes (different phases/dockets of an expansion program), correctly split by GEM, not duplicates or re-filings.

SPEC caveat (documented, not a concern -- both EIA 'differs' flags in the prompt's comparison table resolve in favor of the sheet's recorded values): (1) Capacity: EIA's own Jul2025 and Oct2025 releases state 4600 MMcf/d for this exact project (docket CP21-465, Phase 2, 32.4 mi, 42in, $426M) -- an EXACT match to GEM -- and the operator's own page independently states 'Line 300 - Phase 2 ... Approximately 4.6 Bcf/d.' EIA's LATER releases (2026-01 onward) revised the figure down to 2200 MMcf/d with no accompanying explanation; since this contradicts both the operator's primary statement and EIA's own immediately-prior two releases, the 4600 MMcf/d figure on the sheet is retained as REFS_ADDED (rule 7: a source agreeing with the recorded value is a ref, and the later EIA revision is treated as the outlier, not corrected against). (2) StartYear1: GEM's 2027 matches the FERC Nov 13, 2024 extension-of-time notice for CP21-465 specifically, which requested extension to October 21, 2027, AND matches EIA's own Jul2025/Oct2025/Jan2026 releases (year_in_service=2027 for this exact docket). EIA's LATER releases (May2026, Aug2026) show 2029 for this row, but that figure lines up exactly with a DIFFERENT docket's extension (CP17-117/CP17-118, the original mainline+terminal project, whose own Oct 2023 joint extension request with Driftwood LNG LLC was granted Feb 15 2024 to April 18, 2029) -- and in EIA's Aug2026 release, ALL THREE Line 200/300 phase rows plus the original mainline row cluster at 2029 except Phase 1 (already under construction) at 2028, consistent with EIA having applied the terminal's 2029 milestone broadly rather than tracking CP21-465's actual, more advanced Phase-2-specific 2027 extension. Conclusion: GEM's StartYear1=2027 is correct and better-sourced than EIA's 2026-vintage figure; no change recommended, but flagged here so a future sweep does not 'fix' it toward 2029 off EIA's later releases without re-checking the docket.
